A highly contagious skin infestation caused by the mite Sarcoptes scabiei, causing intense pruritus and a characteristic rash, with crusted scabies occurring in immunocompromised individuals.
An allergic or immune-mediated reaction presenting as transient raised itchy wheals on the skin, often accompanied by angioedema of deeper tissues.
Skin diseases caused by viral pathogens including herpes simplex virus, human papillomavirus (warts), and molluscum contagiosum.
Skin and subcutaneous diseases not classified under the specific GBD sub-categories, including rare, unspecified, or miscellaneous dermatological conditions.
Diseases affecting the skin and subcutaneous tissue, including inflammatory, infectious, allergic, and degenerative conditions.
A chronic disorder characterised by compulsive alcohol consumption, loss of control over drinking, and continued use despite physical and social harm.
Disorders characterised by compulsive use of illicit or prescription drugs, including opioids, stimulants, and cannabis, with significant harm to health and functioning.

Nicotine dependence is a chronic, relapsing condition characterized by compulsive use of nicotine-containing products (most commonly cigarettes), accompanied by tolerance, a withdrawal syndrome on cessation or reduction, and continued use despite the awareness of harmful consequences.
Disorders characterised by compulsive use of psychoactive substances despite adverse consequences, including alcohol and drug use disorders.
Structural or functional abnormalities present at birth, including chromosomal disorders and congenital malformations of the heart, limbs, and other organs.

pref_label: Endocrine, metabolic, blood, and immune disorders
definition: A heterogeneous group of conditions affecting endocrine glands, metabolic processes, and immune function, including thyroid disease, adrenal disorders, and autoimmune conditions. Exception is diabetes, which is captured under "Diabetes and kidney diseases" and more specifically under "Diabetes mellitus".
Diseases of the female reproductive system, including endometriosis, uterine fibroids, polycystic ovary syndrome, and pelvic inflammatory disease.
Inherited disorders of haemoglobin structure or synthesis, including sickle cell disease and thalassaemia, causing haemolytic anaemia and multi-organ complications.
Conditions affecting the teeth, gums, and oral mucosa, including dental caries, periodontal disease, edentulism, and oral infections.
The sudden unexpected death of an apparently healthy infant, typically during sleep, for which no cause is identified after thorough post-mortem investigation.
Conditions affecting the urinary tract and male reproductive system, including urinary tract infections, kidney stones, and causes of male infertility.
Non-communicable diseases not classified under the major GBD NCD categories, including congenital, genitourinary, haematological, and other miscellaneous conditions.
Chronic, non-infectious diseases of long duration including cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic, neurological, and neoplastic conditions.
Injuries and deaths resulting from organised collective violence, including war, armed conflict, and terrorist attacks.
Physical, sexual, or psychological harm intentionally inflicted by one person on another, including assault, domestic violence, and sexual violence.
Deaths and injuries resulting from the use of force by law enforcement or state actors, including fatal police encounters and state-sanctioned executions.
Intentional injury directed at oneself, including suicidal behaviour and non-suicidal self-injury, across a spectrum from ideation to fatal self-inflicted harm.
Intentional injuries caused by violence directed at oneself or others, including self-harm, assault, sexual violence, and conflict-related injuries.
Injuries sustained in road traffic crashes involving motor vehicles, motorcycles, cyclists, and pedestrians.
Harm resulting from medical or surgical interventions, including adverse drug reactions, surgical complications, and healthcare-associated infections.
Injuries caused by contact with animals, including bites, stings, and envenomation from snakes, insects, marine animals, and other wildlife.
Respiratory impairment resulting from submersion or immersion in liquid, including fatal drowning and non-fatal near-drowning events.
Injury caused by passage of electrical current through the body, including low-voltage electrocution and lightning strike, causing tissue damage, cardiac arrest, and burns.
Injuries resulting from exposure to extreme environmental temperatures, including heat stroke, heat exhaustion, hypothermia, and frostbite.
Injuries directly caused by natural forces including earthquakes, floods, storms, landslides, and volcanic eruptions.
Injuries caused by physical mechanical forces including crushing, cutting, impact, and blast, covering occupational and other unintentional mechanical trauma.
Injuries resulting from a person falling from one level to another or on the same level, including fractures, head injuries, and soft tissue trauma.
Injuries to the skin and deeper tissues caused by flames, hot surfaces, scalding liquids, or contact with hot substances.
Injury caused by a foreign object entering the body through ingestion, aspiration, or direct penetration of a body cavity or tissue.
Injury or death resulting from exposure to toxic substances, including medications, household chemicals, pesticides, and environmental toxins.
Unintentional injuries not classified under the specific GBD sub-categories, including other accidental exposures and miscellaneous traumatic events.
Injuries that occur without intent to cause harm, including falls, drowning, burns, poisonings, and environmental exposures.
Physical harm to the body resulting from external causes, including unintentional injuries, self-harm, interpersonal violence, and conflict.
